description: Phase 4: Player Invites + Logout - Implement bookie logout functionality and player invite system where bookies generate unique codes for players to claim their accounts. IMPORTANT: Maintain the existing dark sports-betting theme styling (Theme.swift).

userStories.title: Add Logout Button to Settings
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to logout from the app so I can sign in with a different account.
acceptanceCriteria: Add new 'Account' section to SettingsView.swift before the 'About' section
Add 'Log Out' button with destructive style (red text)
Show confirmation alert before logging out: 'Are you sure you want to log out?'
On confirm: call authManager.signOut() to sign out from Supabase
Handle logout errors gracefully with error alert
After logout, user should see the login screen (AuthGateView handles this)
Use Theme styling for consistency
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Simple addition to existing SettingsView - inject AuthManager via @EnvironmentObject

userStories.title: Add Invite Code Fields to Player Model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need invite code fields on the Player model to track invitation status.
acceptanceCriteria: Add inviteCode: String? field to Player model - unique 8-character alphanumeric code
Add inviteCodeGeneratedAt: Date? field - when the code was generated
Add inviteCodeExpiresAt: Date? field - when the code expires (optional, nil = never)
Add claimedAt: Date? field - when the player claimed their account
Add authUserId: UUID? field - links to Supabase auth user after claim
Update Player initializer to include new fields with nil defaults
Existing players will have nil invite codes (unclaimed legacy players)
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Prepares the model for invite system - needs migration in Supabase later

userStories.title: Create Invite Code Generator Service
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a service to generate and validate unique invite codes.
acceptanceCriteria: Create InviteCodeService.swift in Booki/Services/
Add generateCode() -> String that creates 8-character alphanumeric code (uppercase letters + digits, excluding confusing chars like 0/O, 1/I/L)
Add generateInviteForPlayer(player: Player, expiresIn: TimeInterval?) -> assigns code to player
Add validateCode(_ code: String) async -> Player? that looks up player by invite code
Add revokeCode(for player: Player) that clears the invite code fields
Inject ModelContext for SwiftData queries
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Stateless service - use for both generating and validating codes

userStories.title: Add Generate Invite UI to Player Detail
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to generate an invite code for a player so they can claim their account.
acceptanceCriteria: Find the player detail/edit view (likely PlayerDetailView or similar)
Add 'Invite Code' section showing current invite status
If no code: show 'Generate Invite Code' button
If code exists and not claimed: show code with copy button, show 'Revoke Code' button
If claimed: show 'Account Claimed' with claimed date, no generate button
Copy button copies code to clipboard with haptic feedback
Show code in large, easily readable format (monospace font)
Use Theme styling
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: UI for bookies to manage player invite codes

userStories.title: Create Player Claim View
userStories.description: As a player, I want to enter my invite code to claim my account.
acceptanceCriteria: Create PlayerClaimView.swift in Booki/Views/
Show text field for entering 8-character invite code
Auto-capitalize input and strip non-alphanumeric characters
Show 'Claim Account' button, disabled until 8 characters entered
On submit: validate code via InviteCodeService
If valid: show player name and 'This is you!' confirmation
If invalid/expired: show error message
After confirmation: create Supabase auth account for player
Set player.claimedAt and player.authUserId after successful claim
Use Theme styling with same dark aesthetic
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Entry point for players to claim their account

userStories.title: Add Player Login Option to Auth Flow
userStories.description: As a player, I want to access the player login from the main auth screen.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify AuthGateView to support both bookie and player auth flows
Add 'I'm a Player' link/button below the bookie login form in LoginView
Add playerClaim case to AuthViewType enum
Tapping 'I'm a Player' shows PlayerClaimView
Add 'Back to Bookie Login' link in PlayerClaimView
After player claims account, they should be able to login with email/password
Add player-specific login flow that sets userRole = .player
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Extends existing auth flow - bookie and player share login but claim is player-only

userStories.title: Create Player Main View
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see my bets and balance after logging in.
acceptanceCriteria: Create PlayerMainView.swift in Booki/Views/
Show player's name and current balance prominently at top
Show list of player's active bets (pending, accepted status)
Show list of player's settled bets (win/loss/push)
Show recent ledger entries (deposits, withdrawals, bet settlements)
Add 'Log Out' button that calls authManager.signOut()
Use Theme styling with same dark aesthetic
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Read-only view for players - they see their activity but can't modify bookie data

userStories.title: Route Player to PlayerMainView After Login
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to route authenticated players to their view instead of bookie view.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify AuthGateView to check authManager.userRole after authentication
If userRole == .bookie: show ContentView (existing bookie app)
If userRole == .player: show PlayerMainView
AuthManager should determine role by checking if user has bookie record or player record
Add method to AuthManager: determineUserRole() that queries both tables
On login: first try to find bookie record, if not found try player record
Set appropriate role and ID (currentBookieId or currentPlayerId)
Project builds and runs in Simulator
userStories.notes: Role-based routing - same auth system, different views
